a randomized controlled trial was undertaken to compare four different strategies to provide low vision rehabilitation services in India.

a RCT to compare the effectiveness and efficiency of four different strategies of delivering low vision rehabilitation services was designed and the baseline characteristics of the participants were described.
In summary, our research is concerned with
assessing the effectiveness of different models of delivery of low vision rehabilitation services in a developing country.
assessing the effectiveness of different strategies for delivering low vision rehabilitation services to people with age-related vision loss in India.
the following questions: What are the effectiveness of different strategies to deliver services for individuals with low vision?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
center based rehabilitation, home-based rehabilitation, a mix center-based and home-based rehabilitation and center based rehabilitation plus home-based supplementary visits are equally effective.
all four arms were comparable and that the study design and methodology was sound.
all strategies are effective in delivering low vision rehabilitation services to individuals with vision loss.

the study design was successful in recruiting a sample of individuals with age-related vision loss that was representative of the population from which they were drawn.
center based rehabilitation is as effective as home based rehabilitation.
